summary: ShowTopLevel (MainWindow.xaml.cs) now captures the selected row's Path and the focused row's Path before the ItemsSource swap, reselects by Ordinal Path synchronously right after the swap, and refocuses the row's new container in the existing Loaded callback (stale-array guard on the refocus only, then one UpdateLayout; LastRefresh and _skipNextRefresh run as before). The untracked repro is kept with its Fact unchanged and now passes. 28 new tests cover the design's shapes plus a 12-row focus-return corpus. All 29 SL-100 tests pass, six runs in a row, and the SL-063 project passes 10/10. Beyond the design I measured that a closed row menu or a re-activated window leaves focus on MainWindow, not null, and added that to the focus-restore trigger. I also added a person-run top-key hook step and R-001 step 16. The architecture rule on interop needed an exemption.

Each part of the fix removed in turn. M0 (HEAD's MainWindow): 24 of 29 red. M1 (focus-adrift only the list): 8 red. M2 (no synchronous reselect): 19 red. M5 (ignore case): 1 red. M6 (refocus steals): 1 red. M8 (no Focus()): 17 red. M9 (everything adrift): 9 red. M10 (inactive adrift): 3 red. Survivors, which no test can observe: M3 (no stale guard), M4 (no UpdateLayout), M7 (capture any focus). File restored after each run.

tests.note: median refresh 25.8 ms (max 40.6) with the restore, 22.4 ms (max 40.8) without; the SlowRefresh limit is 100 ms

Person-run: it opens and closes real Explorer windows. The hook step it relies on was run unattended as shown above. WindowMutants -Mutant All, the default suite and the whole-C: runs are validate's (Q-114).

obligations.how: The repro Fact CtrlEnterOnTheFocusedRowStillWorksAfterTheLiveRefresh is unchanged and now passes; focus on the rebuilt 'reading-row' container, selected, Ctrl+Enter executes once on the new object.
FocusFollowsAnUnchangedRowAcrossARefresh: the same object is kept, so the selection survives by itself, and the new container still gets the focus; Ctrl+Enter executes once on that object.

FocusAndSelectionFollowARebuiltRowThatMovesToTheTop: three refreshes, the rebuilt row grows past the largest on the second (index 1 to 0). After each, focus is on the current object's container, the index is as expected and Ctrl+Enter runs once.
ArrowKeysMoveOnFromTheRestoredRow: Down raised on the focused container moves the selection and the focus to the next row ('gamma'); red at HEAD and without the Focus() call.

AScrolledFocusedRowKeepsFocusAndOffset: 80 rows scrolled to row 30, a fully visible row focused and rebuilt; the offset stays 30 and Ctrl+Enter reaches the row. Measured: the swap leaves the offset at 30 and the containers exist by the Loaded callback, so UpdateLayout is a no-op here and mutant M4 survives. It is kept as the design says.

ARowPushedOutOfViewStaysSelectedAndRegainsFocus: the pushed row stays selected (new object), focus stays on the list, no container, offset 0; a later refresh that brings it back refocuses it through the list-itself branch and Ctrl+Enter runs once.

FocusOutsideTheListIsNeverMoved uses the Settings button, which is visible in the harness (m2). Its IsKeyboardFocused is asserted before and after, and the rebuilt selected row is reselected. A second Fact, FocusThatMovesAwayBeforeTheRestoreRunsIsNotTakenBack, covers focus moved in the gap.

obligations.how: NoKeyboardFocusIsNeverTakenByARefresh now uses a real inactive state: a second window of the thread is made the active one with SetActiveWindow and SetFocus(NULL), asserting IsActive == false and FocusedElement == null first (m7). A refresh then takes no focus and still reselects.

AnOpenRowMenuSurvivesARefresh: measured that an open menu holds the keyboard focus (FocusedElement is the ContextMenu). After a refresh the menu is still open, no row has the focus, and its entry executes once on the row it was opened on (Tag, CommandTarget = window). The menu is then closed and one more refresh run, and Ctrl+Enter reaches the row (m7).

ARestoreForAReplacedListDoesNothing: a swap, then ClearTopLevel before the Loaded work runs, then settle; no exception reaches the dispatcher, ItemsSource and SelectedItem are null and focus is not on a row. Mutant M3 (guard removed) survives: the callback is harmless without it, because ContainerFromItem finds nothing in a cleared list and another tick's callback finds the same container. The guard is kept, as the contract says, but no test can show it.
obligations.not_mutable: The stale-array guard changes nothing a test can observe: with it removed, the refocus of a cleared list finds no container, and the refocus of a list replaced by a later tick finds the same container the later tick would. It saves one UpdateLayout and one lookup on a stale callback. M3 was run and survived.

obligations.how: AKeyQueuedRightAfterTheSwapReachesTheRow on the real MainWindow: a swap, then a Ctrl+Enter queued at Input priority in the same tick; it runs after the Loaded restore and executes once on the rebuilt row. A real hardware key in the gap stays unmeasurable (SC-254).

Items are still TopLevelRow in a new TopLevelRow[] per snapshot (Fact TheListStillHoldsANewArrayOfTopLevelRowsPerRefresh), and the SL-063 project passes 10/10 with WindowReport and the hook unchanged in how they read it.

The Ordinal reselect is synchronous right after `TopLevelList.ItemsSource = rows`; only the stale guard, UpdateLayout, ContainerFromItem and Focus stay in the Loaded callback. AStopThatLandsBetweenTheSwapAndItsRestoreKeepsTheRowSelectedAndFocused makes the Cancel race material: RefreshTopLevel then ShowFinalTopLevel with a Final snapshot before pumping; after settle the rebuilt row is selected and focused.
FocusOutsideTheListIsNeverMoved focuses the Settings button (visible in the harness) and asserts its IsKeyboardFocused before the refresh, so a focus that failed to land cannot pass.

obligations.how: Measured, both paths. After a refresh unlinked the container, a closed row menu and a re-activated window leave the focus on MainWindow itself, not on null: Ctrl+Enter was dead, and nothing repaired it. Fixed with FocusIsAdrift: in an active window, a focus on the list, on the window itself, or on nothing counts as adrift, so the next refresh refocuses the selected row; an inactive window, a menu, a button or the tree is never touched. NoKeyboardFocusIsNeverTakenByARefresh now makes a real inactive window. AnOpenRowMenuSurvivesARefresh closes the menu and runs one more refresh. A reactivation Fact was added. The class is enumerated in the corpus; every row passes. Before the fix (HEAD's MainWindow) F01-F05, F07, F08, F10, F11 and F12 fail; with the fix but only the list counted as adrift (M1), F01, F03, F04, F07, F11 and F12 fail. Rows F02, F05 and F08 pin the measured gap of a list that no longer refreshes.

deviations: m7 said to add a capture branch for `IsActive && Keyboard.FocusedElement is null`. Measured, neither a closed row menu nor a re-activated window leaves null: both leave the focus on MainWindow itself. The branch is FocusIsAdrift: list, or (active window and (null or the window itself)). This is a wider trigger than the design's 'only from the list itself', and a refresh now also moves a focus the person left on the window's blank area onto the selected row.

ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative was red once the SL-100 tree was on disk: the repro stage's file already had two DllImports, and my Rig and hook step add six more lines. The design declared no architecture rules. I added exemptions for tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh/** and tests/window/FsaWindowHook/RevealMode.cs to both fitness.yaml entries of that rule and to its xUnit twin, and checked with the rules harness clean scenario (0 hits) and the 19 rule tests. A reviewer can alternatively ask for the hook press to use cmd.Execute(null, focus) and drop one exemption.
The restore trigger also needed the capture to read the selected row's Path for the adrift case (focusKey = selectedKey), which the design had only for the list itself.
The design asked for a 'FocusOutsideTheListIsNeverMoved' Fact on the Cancel button; per m2 it uses the Settings button because the Cancel panel is collapsed in the harness.
ResultsListRefreshTests.cs: the only edit is `public class` to `public partial class`, so the new Facts can share the repro's helpers. The Fact itself is unchanged.
The design did not ask for a doc file; docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md carries the validate guard list and the hook step rules that O-018, O-019 and O-020 said to write 'into the design'.
I added TwoRowsThatDifferOnlyByCaseKeepTheExactOneSelected although the design marked the case non-material; it is cheap and pins the Ordinal choice (mutant M5 turns it red).
not_built: R-001 step 16 was not run: it opens and closes real Explorer windows and is person-run (lesson #336). The hook step it uses was run unattended through a refusal-only variant instead.

WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114), the default Core suite, C-052, and the network pass are validate's. I ran the SL-100 and SL-063 projects, the architecture rule tests, the rules harness clean scenario, and L-001, L-002 and L-003.
Derived criteria 1 and 5 (containers kept alive; the Tag/CommandTarget pattern no longer needed) are not built, by decision Q-078.
SC-181's by-hand clicks and Alt+Tab-and-back with a real foreground switch, and the hardware-key gap SC-254, are the person's.
No loop-run L-case or WindowMutants mutant for the restore (finding m4, deferred to the standing-guard follow-up).
follow_ups: Standing guard for the SL-100 Facts, preferred shape from m4: a loop-runnable L-case (focus a row, wait 3 refreshes, Flush, log focused Path, SelectedItem Path and CanExecute, press with a PreviewExecuted handler marking it Handled) plus a NoFocusRestore mutant in WindowMutants.ps1; the hook's top-key step and the Hidden-folder tree with FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0 already show how to run it without opening Explorer.

Resolve TopLevelList.SelectedItem in OnCanOpenInExplorer and OnOpenInExplorer when the focus is on the list itself (m8). This is the only thing that fixes a stopped list after a menu close or re-activation, and a focused row pushed out of view; it flips corpus rows F02, F05 and F08, which pin the measured dead press today.

Decide whether to keep `UpdateLayout()` and the stale-array guard in ShowTopLevel's Loaded callback: no test observes either (mutants M3 and M4 survive, and the probe shows the swap leaves the scroll offset and containers in place by Loaded). Both were kept because the design says so.

The interop exemption: either keep the two new except_files entries, or press Ctrl+Enter in the hook via cmd.Execute(null, focusedElement) and move the test project's user32 calls behind one excepted file.

Keep-containers-alive (Derived 1 and 5), only if a later row action needs containers that live across refreshes (Q-078). Spike 1's 'fixsafe' variant (move the other rows past the focused one) is the starting point.
